text: Ṣé mo lè gba iná fún fóònù mi?
ipa: ʃe˥ mo le˩ ɡba ina˥ fũ˥ fo˥o˩nu˩ mi

text: Mo fẹ́ yàrá tí a kò fi mu sìgá
ipa: mo fɛ˥ ja˩ra˥ ti˥ a ko˩ fi mu si˩ɡa˥

text: Mo fẹ́ yàrá tí ó dákẹ́
ipa: mo fɛ˥ ja˩ra˥ ti˥ o˥ da˥kɛ˥

text: Ṣé oúnjẹ àárọ̀ wà nínú owó náà?
ipa: ʃe˥ oũ˥dʒɛ a˩a˥rɔ˩ wa˩ ni˥nu˥ owo˥ na˥a˩

text: Ṣé mo lè wo yàrá náà?
ipa: ʃe˥ mo le˩ wo ja˩ra˥ na˥a˩

text: Ṣé mo lè jáde nígbà tí ó yá?
ipa: ʃe˥ mo le˩ dʒa˥de ni˥ɡba˩ ti˥ o˥ ja˥

text: Wákàtí mélòó ni oúnjẹ àárọ̀ ń bẹ̀rẹ̀?
ipa: wa˥ka˩ti˥ me˥lo˩o˥ ni oũ˥dʒɛ a˩a˥rɔ˩ n̩˥ bɛ˩rɛ˩

text: Ṣé mo lè fi ẹrù mi pamọ́?
ipa: ʃe˥ mo le˩ fi ɛru˩ mi kpamɔ˥

text: Ẹ má ṣe wẹ̀ yàrá yìí
ipa: ɛ ma˥ ʃe wɛ˩ ja˩ra˥ ji˩i˥

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, aṣọ ìnú omi mìíràn
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, aʃɔ i˩nu˥ omi mi˩i˥rã˩

text: Ṣé mo lè dúró òru mìíràn?
ipa: ʃe˥ mo le˩ du˥ro˥ o˩ru mi˩i˥rã˩

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, ẹ jí mi ní {}
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ɛ dʒi˥ mi ni˥ {}

text: Ìṣòro kan wà pẹ̀lú yàrá náà
ipa: i˩ʃo˩ro kã wa˩ kpɛ˩lu˥ ja˩ra˥ na˥a˩

text: Ṣé mo lè yí yàrá padà?
ipa: ʃe˥ mo le˩ ji˥ ja˩ra˥ kpada˩

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, ẹ rán ẹnìkan wá láti tún un ṣe
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ɛ rã˥ ɛni˩kã wa˥ la˥ti tũ˥ ũ ʃe

text: Ìgbà wo ni yóò ti ṣe?
ipa: i˩ɡba˩ wo ni jo˥o˩ ti ʃe

text: Ṣé ó lè ṣe tán lónìí?
ipa: ʃe˥ o˥ le˩ ʃe tã˥ lo˥ni˩i˥

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, má ṣe lo bilíṣì
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ma˥ ʃe lo bili˥ʃi˩

text: Ẹ dúró, ẹ má ṣe tẹ̀síwájú
ipa: ɛ du˥ro˥, ɛ ma˥ ʃe tɛ˩si˥wa˥dʒu˥
literal: stop, do not continue -- two clauses for the Mandarin row's reason and more sharply here, because Yoruba dúró covers stop and wait alike (this pack uses it for both common-signs.stopped-stop and communication.please-wait-a-moment), so the terminality has to be carried by tẹ̀síwájú rather than by the verb

stop for a minute -- the duration is what says temporarily, since the verb cannot; built from this pack's own board-answers.please-wait (ìṣẹ́jú kan) and border-customs.i-am-staying-for-days (dúró fún)

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, má ṣe fọwọ́ kàn ibi yìí
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ma˥ ʃe fɔwɔ˥ kã˩ ibi ji˩i˥
literal: please do not touch this spot -- fọwọ́ kàn, to touch with the hand, from this pack's common-signs.do-not-touch, in the negative-imperative frame of its laundry.please-do-not-use-bleach. Touch rather than press: no pressure-specific verb could be sourced with tone marks

text: Ẹ fi agbára díẹ̀ kún un
ipa: ɛ fi aɡba˥ra di˥ɛ˩ kũ˥ ũ
literal: please add a little force to it -- the same reading as the Mandarin 用力一点, built from this pack's utility-templates.please-do-not-add (fi {} kún un) and its agbára. Six words against the two of Ẹ rọra, because neither button carries a labelKey on the spa board and the owner's own wording is what labels them, side by side

gently -- rọra is rọ̀ (to be soft) plus ara (body), so it is not purely a speed word, but it does also carry carefully and slowly and Yoruba gives no pressure-specific comparative pair of the kind German, Finnish and Russian have. The weakest row in this set; a fluent speaker should read it first

text: Ó dára bẹ́ẹ̀, ẹ máa tẹ̀síwájú
ipa: o˥ da˥ra bɛ˥ɛ˩, ɛ ma˥a tɛ˩si˥wa˥dʒu˥
literal: it is good like that, carry on -- a confirmation with a keep-it-there clause, not praise; Ó dára from this pack's board-answers.stay-here and bẹ́ẹ̀ from its slang.seriously

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, ẹ lo àkókò púpọ̀ lórí èjìká
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ɛ lo a˩ko˥ko˩ kpu˥kpɔ˩ lo˥ri˥ e˩dʒi˩ka˥
literal: please spend a lot of time on the shoulders -- the concept's own reading, since Yoruba has no single settled noun for massage as a bookable service: Glosbe gives the coinages ìpara oníwòsàn and ìpara ìtunilára, and Nigerian spas advertise in English

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, ẹ lo àkókò púpọ̀ lórí ẹ̀yìn
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ɛ lo a˩ko˥ko˩ kpu˥kpɔ˩ lo˥ri˥ ɛ˩jĩ˩

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, ẹ lo àkókò púpọ̀ lórí ọrùn
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ɛ lo a˩ko˥ko˩ kpu˥kpɔ˩ lo˥ri˥ ɔrũ˩
literal: no single Yoruba term grouping the neck with the shoulders could be sourced, so the two rows stand apart on their own words

text: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, ẹ lo àkókò púpọ̀ lórí àtẹ́lẹ̀sẹ̀
ipa: ɛ dʒɔ˩wɔ˥, ɛ lo a˩ko˥ko˩ kpu˥kpɔ˩ lo˥ri˥ a˩tɛ˥lɛ˩sɛ˩
literal: àtẹ́lẹ̀sẹ̀, the sole, as this pack's body-parts.foot already has it, because ẹsẹ̀ alone is the whole leg

text: Ó dára, mi ò fọwọ́ kàn ibi yìí
ipa: o˥ da˥ra, mi o˩ fɔwɔ˥ kã˩ ibi ji˩i˥
literal: all right, I do not touch this spot -- Yoruba has no gender anywhere in the grammar, so no reply in this set needed steering. Written with the unmarked verb rather than the negative future mi ò ní, which would read as I do not have a hand next to fọwọ́
which spot exactly -- wo from this pack's transit-rides.what-is-the-next-stop and gan-an from its question-words.very

text: Ìtọ́jú yìí kò ṣeé ṣe láì fọwọ́ kàn ibi yìí
ipa: i˩tɔ˥dʒu˥ ji˩i˥ ko˩ ʃee˥ ʃe la˥i˩ fɔwɔ˥ kã˩ ibi ji˩i˥
literal: this treatment cannot be done without touching this spot -- kò ṣeé ṣe from this pack's board-answers.not-possible and láì from its dietary-needs.no-meat

text: Ṣé ibi yìí ń dùn yín?
ipa: ʃe˥ ibi ji˩i˥ n̩˥ dũ˩ jĩ˥
literal: does this spot hurt -- ń dùn from this pack's emergency-medical.it-hurts-here, and the formal yín its board-answers.what-is-your-name already uses

text: Mi ò mọ̀, màá béèrè lọ́wọ́ ọ̀gá
ipa: mi o˩ mɔ˩, ma˩a˥ be˥e˩re˩ lɔ˥wɔ˥ ɔ˩ɡa˥
literal: I do not know, I will ask the boss -- ọ̀gá is used of a superior of any sex and is the source of Nigerian Pidgin oga; Mi ò mọ̀ is this pack's social-basics.i-do-not-know verbatim
